what: The GPU reference denominator for a Tenstorrent port of Nesso-1. Nesso-1 predicts protein-ligand binding AFFINITY only -- no structure, no pose -- so the output guard is on the affinity scalars, and the validity check is a correlation against measured Kd, not an RMSD.
box: vast.ai offer 48180701, machine 39919, Washington US, on-demand $4.111/hr incl. 80GB disk, contract 48201689, GPU-6cf32d44

headline.primary_metric: predictions_per_hour (screen leg, one target x many compounds)
headline.why: Affinity prediction is virtual screening: one target against millions of compounds. The number that decides whether a port is worth building is throughput at the concurrency the tool admits, not the latency of one prediction. s/prediction is reported at every rung as the secondary metric and is what a matched TT-vs-GPU cell must compare.

target_definition.rule: tt_target_s = 4 * the H200 number at the SAME rung and the SAME batch
target_definition.why: The org bar is within 4x of one H200 per chip at matched batch, the same bar as one 32-chip Galaxy beating one 8-GPU DGX H200.
target_definition.matched_batch: Nesso-1 admits exactly one batch size. The dataloader hardcodes batch_size=1 and the crop path is structurally batch-1, so every cell here is batch 1 and a TT cell is comparable only at batch 1. The throughput lever is process concurrency, measured separately.
target_definition.which_kernel_arm: Score the port against the KERNELS-ON arm. cuEquivariance is on by default in the shipped checkpoint (hparams use_kernels: true), so it is what a user gets, and a reference measured with it off would flatter the port. The off arm is recorded so the cost of the CUDA-only kernels -- which have no Tenstorrent equivalent -- is visible rather than hidden in the bar.

protocol.reps: 3 per cell in one process; rep 0 discarded as cold; median of the warm reps
protocol.excluded_from_per_prediction: checkpoint load, YAML/RDKit preprocess, and the ESM-2 embedding, all reported separately as fixed_* -- a screening run pays each once per invocation, and the ESM embedding once per unique sequence, not once per compound
protocol.mixed_phase: crop (distogram head, then a device->host sync and a numpy selection)
protocol.refine_protein_inference: on (shipped default), 256-token budget, 22.0 A cutoff. The norefine_* cells are the same ladder with it off.
protocol.msa: none -- Nesso-1 has no MSA input at all
protocol.precision: bf16-mixed (shipped default); the two affinity heads run fp32, autocast disabled upstream, with float32_matmul_precision=highest
protocol.gpu_exclusive: every single-process cell asserts it was the only compute app on the card. In the concurrency cells the other apps are our own workers by construction, so that check is expected to fail there and the other output guards carry the cell.

cli_end_to_end.arm: nesso predict CLI, wall clock around the real command, fresh out_dir every run
cli_end_to_end.note:
The as-shipped `nesso predict` CLI, wall-clocked around the real command, fresh out_dir per run.

Timed the same way as the Boltz-2 arm on purpose: comparing an in-process steady state against a
full CLI invocation would inflate the ratio by one side's entire fixed cost.

An earlier pass of this leg reported 6.43 s for the 64-compound directory and ~5.5 s for a single
record. Neither reproduces: a clean re-run of the identical command took 58.95 s for the same 64
compounds, with Lightning's own progress bar showing 46 s at 1.42 it/s, which agrees with the
in-process steady state of 0.754 s/prediction measured three independent ways. Those figures are
discarded rather than explained.

single_invocation.arm: boltz-2 upstream, single sequence, tt-bio's shipped affinity settings

directory_amortised.arm: boltz-2 upstream over a 4-compound directory, one target, no MSA, tt-bio shipped affinity settings

matched_marginal.method: two measured points per arm, single record and a directory: marginal = (wall_dir - wall_single) / (n_dir - 1). Same card, same 256 aa protein, same ligands, no MSA, one prediction at a time on both arms.
matched_marginal.verdict: Nesso-1 is 19.3x cheaper per screened compound than Boltz-2 affinity at matched protocol, which reproduces the technical report's 10-20x claim at the top of its range.

output_validity.benchmark: DAVIS (TDC), kinase/inhibitor Kd in nM, non-censored only
output_validity.metric: within-target Pearson of predicted pAffinity (= -affinity_pred_value, so higher = stronger, same direction as pKd) against pKd = 9 - log10(Kd_nM)
output_validity.control: molecular weight alone (RDKit Descriptors.MolWt) vs pKd, same ligands
output_validity.verdict: VALID: within-target Pearson 0.636 beats the MW-only control 0.175
